Which Duval County offices matter for a Jacksonville tax bill?

Jacksonville and Duval County share one tax collector. That office mails the bills and takes the payments, while a separate property appraiser decides what each parcel is worth and who qualifies for an exemption.

  • Tax collector: 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202. Call (904) 255-5700 and choose option 4 for property tax. The main office opens weekdays at half past eight and closes at half past four.
  • Property appraiser exemptions desk: (904) 255-5900, for homestead status and address changes.
  • Value Adjustment Board clerk: 117 West Duval Street, Suite 305, for formal appeals.

Branch offices are spread across the city, and the Kernan and Hogan locations were replaced in 2026 by a St. Johns Square branch at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121. Confirm the branch list and hours before you go in person, because office locations changed during 2026.

What are the Jacksonville payment months and discounts?

Jacksonville tax is figured on the January 1 value, mailed in November and due in full by March 31. Each month of waiting trims the discount.

Early payment months printed on the Duval County Tax Collector Real Estate Taxes page (taxcollector.jacksonville.gov)
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone

A Jacksonville house that goes under contract in spring has usually already been billed. Ask which discount tier the seller used and whether the payment cleared.

What does Duval County do with delinquent Jacksonville accounts?

Unpaid accounts on April 1 carry a mandatory minimum interest fee of 3%, plus advertising costs. Whatever remains goes into the annual tax certificate sale, which must happen on or before June 1.

The 2026 Duval sale was set for May 27, with online registration opening May 8. The collector describes the rules bidders live by:

  • The lowest interest rate wins, and ties are settled by random draw.
  • A deposit of $100 or 10% of intended bids, whichever is larger, must arrive five business days before the sale.
  • Winners pay within 48 hours or lose the deposit.
  • A certificate redeemed early pays the buyer at least 5%, whatever the bid was.
  • A certificate expires if no tax deed application follows within seven years.

For an owner, two lines on the same page matter more. Homestead liens are excluded from the certificate sale, and the Clerk of Court, not the collector, conducts tax deed sales. The collector also warns that a tax deed is not a warranty deed, so a buyer at that sale may have to clear title through a court action.

How does the Duval installment plan work?

If your estimated bill tops $100, you can split it into four payments, provided you apply by April 30 of the year you want to start. Applications go in through your online account, by email to taxdept@coj.net, or by mail to Installment Processing at the Forsyth Street office.

  • First payment: June 30, 6% discount.
  • Second payment: September 30, 4.5% discount.
  • Third payment: December 31, 3% discount.
  • Fourth payment: March 31, no discount.

A July 31 row offers a late first payment with no discount. Miss that too and the account leaves the plan without penalty and is billed in November. After the first payment, you are committed for the rest of the year, and a skipped installment is folded into the next with no discount. Enrolled accounts re-enter each year automatically. Owners who want to pay only part of a bill outside the plan are told by the Value Adjustment Board page to speak to the tax collector first.

How can I dispute a Jacksonville valuation or exemption?

A petition to the Value Adjustment Board has to arrive within 25 days of the mailing of your TRIM notice. The due date is printed in the lower right corner of the notice, and a postmark does not count: the board needs to physically receive the petition and fee by then.

The 2026 cutoff fell on Tuesday, September 8, and the online option shut at 11:59 p.m. that night. That window has closed. In other years expect the same rhythm of an August notice and a September deadline. A late petition must come by hand or mail with a written good-cause explanation and documents.

  • Fee: up to $50 per parcel, not refundable.
  • Waiver: a homeowner who appeals a homestead denial on time pays nothing.
  • Form: DR-486, available from the board, the appraiser or the state.
  • Panel: two City Council members, one school board member and two citizens.

The appraiser invites an informal review first but cannot accept a petition itself.

Why can two similar Jacksonville houses carry different bills?

The Duval appraiser's FAQ answers this directly: tax rates are usually the same, but taxable value differs. A long-time homesteader's assessed value has been held down by the Save Our Homes cap, which the state chart sets at 2.7 percent for 2026, while a recent buyer pays on full market value.

The same FAQ explains several surprises. A partial homestead exemption can come from multiple owners, mixed use or several buildings. A bank-sold house is still valued at market, because foreclosures and distressed sales are not treated as qualified sales. A homestead can show a rising assessed value even when market value fell, until the gap built up by the cap is used up.

When you sell, expect the buyer's first bill to climb. The change of ownership removes the cap, and the exemption has to be reapplied for by March 1. The standard homestead exemption is up to $50,000, filed on DR-501.

How do I settle Jacksonville tax when the house sells?

Ask the tax collector for a written payoff and pass it to the title company. The closing agent subtracts what is owed and apportions the current year across both parties. Anyone on the installment plan should ask the collector what happens to the remaining payments.

  • Ask whether the account carries back taxes or a certificate.
  • Check the bill for non-ad valorem lines such as stormwater and solid waste.
  • Search the clerk's Official Records for recorded liens.

Florida's deed stamp tax runs 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and any party named on the deed can be held liable for it. Recording is priced under s. 28.24: $5.00 on page one, $4.00 on each later page, and added per-page charges.

A seller facing back tax or damage may prefer a cash buyer who accepts the house as-is, with the title company clearing the tax from proceeds.

Where do I find the Jacksonville millage rate?

No rate appears on the collector's millage page. It sends readers to the Property Appraiser, which posts the charts. A mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value, and your parcel's total adds up each district's rate. Use your own bill or that chart rather than a citywide guess.

More questions about Jacksonville, FL Property Tax Guide

When does Jacksonville tax become delinquent?

April 1 of the year after the assessment. A minimum 3% interest fee and advertising costs follow, and unpaid accounts move toward a certificate sale held by June 1.

What discount do I get for paying a Jacksonville bill early?

November payments get 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%. March payments get none.

Are homesteads sold in the Duval tax certificate sale?

No. The collector's page states that homestead liens are not subject to the sale. The tax itself must still be paid.

Who do I call about a Jacksonville bill that looks wrong?

Start with the property appraiser's exemptions line, (904) 255-5900. If that fails, petition the Value Adjustment Board before the notice's printed deadline. Payment plans are a question for the collector.

How is a Jacksonville house's tax divided at closing?

The closing statement shows each side's share, and unpaid back tax comes out of the seller's proceeds. Get the payoff figure in writing beforehand.

Which Miami office sends the tax bill, and which one sets the value?

The Miami-Dade Tax Collector produces and collects the bill. The Property Appraiser of Miami-Dade County produces the values behind it, and says on its home page that it never mails bills or sets and collects taxes. Miami levies its own mills, which appear on the same statement as county, school and special district lines.

A city spread across 36.00 square miles has parcels in different neighborhoods that can sit on different taxing lines, so always work from the folio and not the street address.

  • Appraiser, downtown: Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710, 305-375-4712, weekdays 8 to 5.
  • Appraiser, south: South Dade Government Center, 10710 SW 211 Street, Cutler Bay, 305-232-3810.
  • Tax Collector: payments online at any hour, at 13 locations, or through its T-Connect mobile offices.

Which Miami services can be handled without a trip downtown?

More than the old paper routine suggests. The appraiser now takes widow(er) exemptions and disability exemptions for veterans or surviving spouses online, with document upload, and agricultural classification applications on Form MD-482 can be filed the same way. A tangible personal property search covers business accounts by name, address or folio, and appointments for the downtown and Cutler Bay offices can be booked online.

On the clerk side, a free alert system emails an owner within 24 hours when a deed or mortgage is recorded in their name. A Miami property left vacant after a move or a death is a common target for deed fraud, so owners of such houses should enroll before listing.

What millage does the county's 2026 chart assign to Miami?

The chart lists Miami at 7.1080 mills for city operations plus 0.2536 for city debt, and the row total is 19.9544. The county prints the chart under the title 2026 adopted millage rates. The chart's 2025 column for the same row reads 19.9878, so the combined figure slipped by 0.0334.

A second row covers the downtown development area, where an added 0.3800 brings the total to 20.3344 (20.3778 in 2025). Houses inside that boundary use the second row, so confirm the parcel on the appraiser's site first. Miami Beach also has a second row, at 19.4045 against its main 18.6681.

What does Miami's housing mix mean for a seller?

Fewer than a third of Miami housing units (30.8 percent) are lived in by their owners, so investor-held houses are common. A landlord selling has no homestead relief to lose, and an owner-occupant buying from one can apply after closing. The Census lists a typical owner-reported value of $518,100 and median gross rent of $1,758 for the city.

  • November to February: the discount months, which the Tax Collector promotes as a chance to save 4 percent by paying in November.
  • April 1: unpaid bills are delinquent.

Where does Amendment 3 leave a Miami bill?

The appraiser's home page invites owners to use a property tax estimator tied to the Amendment 3 changes, with separate estimates for 2027 and 2028. Those two years match the amounts in the statewide measure voters passed on November 3, 2026, as the neighboring Seminole and Hillsborough appraisers describe it. The Tax Collector's pay-early campaign, which promotes the 4 percent November discount, applies to the 2026 bill now in hand.

In practice, treat the 2026 bill as unchanged and run the estimator for the year your closing or purchase falls in. A buyer who expects a larger exemption should still file for it, since benefits reach an owner only through an application.

What should a Miami seller collect before the closing table?

Bring four things: the folio number, the August TRIM notice showing proposed taxes, proof of each exemption on file, and a Tax Collector payoff letter for any open year.

A house inside the downtown development area needs the title agent's attention, because it carries the extra 0.3800 mills. Buyers should expect the first bill after purchase to start from just value, which can run well above the seller's bill.

How does a Miami owner claim homestead or port a capped value?

Apply on Form DR-501 by March 1 for a house that was your permanent home on January 1. Renting it ends the benefit. A sale restarts the buyer at just value, and the seller can port savings to a new Florida homestead with Form DR-501T inside three years.

Homestead abuse can be reported to the appraiser's compliance unit at 305-375-3402. An owner who cannot pay can ask the Tax Collector about deferral on Form DR-570 (March 31) or installments (May 1).

What if back taxes are owed on a Miami house?

After April 1 the account is delinquent and a certificate is sold by June 1. The buyer of the certificate has to wait two years before pressing the owner. A tax deed application costs $75, and a homestead parcel's opening bid includes half of the latest assessed value. If no one bids, the county has 90 days to take the land at the opening bid.

A seller with arrears can still close, because the title company pays off the lien from proceeds. Request the payoff early, and call the Tax Collector long before any auction date.

Where are Miami deeds recorded?

At the Miami-Dade County Recorder's Office, 20 NW 1st Avenue, Suite 5.246, run by the county clerk. The clerk's checklist asks for the seller's original signature, two unrelated witnesses with printed names and addresses, a notary acknowledgement and a Prepared By line. Before the notary meeting, compare the folio and legal description with the prior deed, and have the two witnesses' printed names and addresses ready. Deed stamps run 60 cents per $100 here, and the clerk's fraud alert emails an owner within 24 hours of a new recording under their name.

Is Miami's city millage rate 7.1080?

Yes, for city operations on the county's 2026 chart, plus 0.2536 for city debt. All authorities total 19.9544 mills, or 20.3344 on the downtown development line.

Can a Miami landlord claim homestead?

No. The owner must live in the home as a permanent residence by January 1, and renting the unit ends the exemption.

What early payment discount does a Miami bill carry?

It steps down monthly from 4 percent for November to 1 percent for February. March is due at the full amount.

Does the Miami property appraiser collect tax?

No. Its home page says it neither sends bills nor sets or collects taxes. Payments go to the Miami-Dade Tax Collector.

How do I check my Miami taxable value?

Search by address, owner name or folio on the appraiser's site, or call 305-375-4712 to book an assessment review.

Who actually bills a Miami Beach homeowner?

Two county offices and one city office share the work. The county Property Appraiser values the parcel, the county Tax Collector mails the yearly statement and takes payment, and Miami Beach Finance handles the city's own charges: utility invoices, special assessments and Resort Tax.

Finance operates from 1700 Convention Center Drive on weekdays. Its page lists a Finance Department schedule of 9AM to 5PM and a customer service window from 8:30AM to 6PM, with 305.673.7000 as the main number. Resort Tax questions have their own line, 305.673.7420, and an email address on the city's File/Pay Resort Tax page.

  • Valuation, exemption filings and portability: county Property Appraiser.
  • Annual statement, tax certificate sales and 13 locations: county Tax Collector.
  • Water, sewer and storm bills plus assessments on the lot: Miami Beach Finance.
  • Rentals taxed on room revenue: Resort Tax desk at Finance.

Which millage lines does the county print for Miami Beach in 2026?

The Property Appraiser's chart titled 2026 Adopted Millage Rates gives Miami Beach a city operating figure of 5.8060 mills and a voted debt figure of 0.2693 mills. Its main Miami Beach line totals 18.6681. A second line repeats those city numbers, adds 0.7364 under the miscellaneous heading and totals 19.4045. Your bill's district code tells you which line applies.

The remainder of each total is the countywide, school, library, children's trust and regional stack, which is identical for every municipality. That is why the city columns are the part worth comparing.

Where does Miami Beach sit among its neighbors?

The chart puts Miami Beach between Coral Gables and Surfside on the low side and North Miami Beach and Miami on the high side. Reading only the city operating column can mislead: Surfside prints the smallest city rate in the table, yet its overall total is higher than Coral Gables, and Coral Gables posts the lowest total of the six.

Miami Beach also carries a voted debt column, which Coral Gables and Surfside do not show. Barrier-island cities further north, such as Sunny Isles Beach and Bal Harbour, print far smaller city rates, so the oceanfront setting alone says nothing about a bill.

What does a short-term rental in Miami Beach do to a homestead?

It can cost the owner the homestead exemption. The city's Short-term Rental Requirements page lists a written notice that the owner has read and understands that renting the residence short term could end the exemption, and that notice is part of the business tax receipt paperwork.

The same page asks for a long document list, which is useful to anyone buying a Miami Beach unit as an income property:

  • An approved Certificate of Use and a recorded warranty deed or bill of sale.
  • For condos, an association letter dated within the last 60 days confirming short-term rental is allowed for that unit.
  • Names and contacts for every hosting or advertising platform used for the listing.
  • A Resort Tax registration with photo ID and signatures of all operators.
  • A notarized affidavit, returned by mail or in person within two weeks of issuance.

Resort Tax itself is 4 percent on room rent and 2 percent on food and drink sales, according to the Finance page. A buyer underwriting a rental should price that in next to the property tax.

What yearly deadlines matter for a Miami Beach parcel?

The statewide calendar drives it: exemption papers reach the appraiser by March 1, the August mailing shows proposed taxes with a 25-day window to petition on value, and November statements carry a 4 percent early discount that steps down monthly to 1 percent in February.

The Miami-Dade Tax Collector pushes the November date hard, branding it "Save the Max," and lists online payment, 13 locations and T-Connect mobile offices as ways to pay. Anything still open on April 1 goes delinquent, and certificates are sold by June 1.

How does Save Our Homes treat a Miami Beach house?

Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value, filed on Form DR-501. After the first year, assessed value may rise by the smaller of 3 percent or the CPI change, and the state's cap chart shows 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026.

That cap disappears at sale, because the next owner starts at full just value on the following January 1. Sellers who plan a move can instead apply portability on a replacement Florida home, using Form DR-501T within a three-year window.

What gets settled at a Miami Beach closing?

The title agent reconciles the year's county bill, utility balances and any city assessment on the lot. Ask Finance for a payoff on the city items, since the county statement does not show them.

Miami-Dade documents carry their own stamp tax rate: 60 cents per $100 with a 45 cents per $100 surtax that skips a deed conveying only a single-family dwelling. Recording is handled by the Miami-Dade Clerk, and Florida wants two subscribing witnesses on a land conveyance.

Where can a Miami Beach owner read the city's own budget papers?

The Office of Management and Budget page on the city site posts a Budget in Brief, the full operating budget, the City Manager's budget message and a two-volume capital budget for both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2026. It also links the budget amendments and resolutions page, a fee schedule for fiscal 2027 and a 2025 Resort Tax report.

Those files explain what the city's share of the bill pays for. The capital volumes are the first year of a five-year improvement plan, updated annually, so an owner worried about a nearby street or seawall project can look up the schedule instead of guessing. The page says the city has used a performance-based budget method since the fiscal 2006 budget, which ties each department's spending to its work plan.

How do the two Miami Beach lines on the chart affect a buyer?

A buyer comparing two listings should look at the taxing district code and the folio's last bill, not only the city name. The extra 0.7364 on the second line adds roughly four percent to that line's total over the first, and nobody can see it from the street address.

  • Pull the folio from the Property Appraiser and note its district.
  • Match it against the chart's line for Miami Beach.
  • Ask Finance whether a special assessment is recorded against the lot.
  • Use the Tax Collector's calculators to test a purchase price before making an offer.

What do the business tax receipt codes tell a short-term rental buyer?

The city assigns occupational code 95017300 for residential short-term rental and 95017301 for the non-residential version. Which one applies decides which documents the application needs, and a condo cannot get a unit receipt until its association has an active receipt of its own.

Check that the seller's receipt, Resort Tax account and association letter are current before you assume the income transfers. The Finance page also covers the question of how to treat sales through third-party platforms, so the platform names on the listing matter at filing time.

No. The Miami-Dade Tax Collector bills property tax. Miami Beach Finance bills utilities and special assessments and collects Resort Tax.

What are the Miami Beach city millage numbers on the 2026 chart?

The chart shows 5.8060 mills operating and 0.2693 voted debt, with totals of 18.6681 and 19.4045 on its two Miami Beach lines.

Can renting my condo short term affect my homestead?

Yes. The city requires owners to acknowledge in writing that short-term rental use could cause loss of the homestead exemption.

What is the Resort Tax rate in Miami Beach?

The city's Finance page lists 4 percent on room rent and 2 percent on restaurant, bar and nightclub sales.

Who do I ask about a special assessment on my Miami Beach lot?

Miami Beach Finance at 305.673.7000. Its page says the department invoices and collects all special assessments.

The name causes confusion. "Homestead" is this South Florida city and also the Florida exemption for a primary residence, and the two have no automatic link: a Homestead city house must still file for the exemption, and homes across Miami-Dade can claim it too.

When do City of Homestead tax notices arrive and what do early payers save?

The collector's real estate page gives October 30, 2026 as the mailing date for 2026 notices, with online viewing and payment from that day. Payment without penalty runs through March 31.

Checks mailed to the Miami address earn the discount by postmark. Banks' bill-pay services need about five business days, so schedule early and quote the folio number printed on the notice.

What follows a missed deadline in Homestead?

From April 1 the account counts as delinquent and picks up at least 3% interest plus advertising and fee charges. If 2026 tax is not paid before June 1, 2027, the collector says a certificate may issue, and that year's certificate sale is listed as starting June 1, 2027.

The collector warns that a certificate can end in loss of the property down the line. An investor holding the certificate may petition for a deed once two full years pass after the April 1 of issue. At the clerk's auction the winner must put down 5 percent of the bid (or $200 if that is more) and pay the balance and fees within a day.

A local wrinkle: some Miami-Dade bills carry a Water, Road and Sewer assessment collected in 30-year annual installments. The collector states that such a bill must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold on the remaining lien balance. Look for that line on your notice.

How much of the bill can a Homestead exemption remove?

A qualifying owner can lower assessed value by as much as $50,000, in two slices. School taxes see only the first $25,000, and the second slice applies to value above $50,000. Residency on January 1 is a condition, and Form DR-501 is due at the Property Appraiser's office by March 1.

  • The exemption ends if the home is rented out or you stop being a Florida resident.
  • Save Our Homes limits each year's rise in assessed value to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is less. The state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Once title changes hands, the next January 1 brings a reset to just value, with a few spouse and inheritance exceptions.
  • Portability carries some of the capped savings to a new Florida homestead. File DR-501T, and set up the new home within three years of the January 1 after you left the old one.

Buyers can try the Property Appraiser's online tax estimator before an offer.

What can a Homestead owner do about a value or exemption notice?

TRIM notices come from the Property Appraiser each August. Petitions to the Value Adjustment Board are due 25 days after that mailing, and a denied exemption gets 30 days from the denial letter.

File the exemption on time so no appeal is needed. If a refund follows a Property Appraiser or board ruling, the collector's FAQ lists a refund email address for it. A refund arising from a sale is a different matter, handled between buyer and seller at closing.

What do City of Homestead budget announcements say about the rate?

A city post dated October 2, 2026 says the approved FY 2026 to 2027 budget leaves the operating millage rate where it was the year before. The post gives no number, so find the rate on your own notice.

The same announcement mentions $32 million for capital projects and five more police officer positions. Separately, voters were asked on November 4, 2025 to approve two general obligation bonds, one for parks and one for roads. The city's FAQ estimated 0.3661 mills for parks and 0.3983 mills for roadways if all of it were issued, and said borrowing would come in several series. Ask the city whether either bond now appears on your parcel.

Total millage on any parcel is the sum of every taxing district, and the collector's FAQ says to find it on the bill.

How do I pay, and where do I find older tax records?

The collector accepts payment online by check, credit card or debit card, in person by check, cashier's check, money order, certified funds, cash, cards or Apple Pay, and by mailed check. Write the folio number and a phone number on a mailed check, make it payable to the Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector in U.S. funds, and leave out sensitive details.

  • Wire payments: email the collector's wire address listed on its FAQ page for instructions. The collector says a wire takes one to two business days to post.
  • Older bills: the collector says it can supply property tax records older than those online, and the FAQ lists an email address for the request.
  • Escrow: if you are unsure whether your lender is paying, ask the lender directly.
  • Roll changes: the certified tax roll reaches the collector once a year, expected around November 1, so recent ownership or address changes may not show online before then.

The collector's FAQ adds that Florida has no personal property tax on vehicles, which spares a seller who is also moving a car or boat from one more bill.

What should a Homestead seller prepare before closing?

Miami-Dade uses its own deed stamp rate, which the revenue department prints as 60 cents per $100 plus a 45-cent surtax, with the surtax skipped on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Most other counties charge 70 cents per $100. Every party to a document can be held liable.

  • Obtain a written payoff, and ask if a delinquency or certificate notice exists.
  • Learn from the title company how the year will be apportioned.
  • Review the clerk's records for liens and check for a Water, Road and Sewer assessment.
  • Report any quarterly installment payments, since missing the July 31 first-payment cutoff removes the account from the plan.

When back taxes or a title problem would stall a bank-financed buyer, a cash purchase lets the title company clear the debt from proceeds.

The Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector. The city sets a rate but does not send a bill.

When is Homestead real estate tax late?

Once March 31 passes. April 1 brings at least 3% interest plus advertising costs and fees.

Does a tax certificate mean the city takes my house?

Not yet. The certificate is a lien an investor buys, and a deed application cannot come until two years after that April 1.

Do I qualify for the exemption if I move in during the spring?

Not for that year. Residence on January 1 and a March 1 filing are both required, and a sale resets the buyer's assessed value the next January 1.

Does the City of Homestead add its own transfer tax?

The city's pages do not list one, so confirm with the city. The state deed stamp tax applies at the Miami-Dade rate the revenue department prints.

The Tax Collector's office handles payments at 813-635-5200 and through HillsTaxFL.gov, with drop boxes and service centers. Tampa City Council adopted a rate of 6.2076 mills for fiscal year 2026 through Resolution 2025-813, passed 6 to 0 at the council meeting. The resolution levies that rate on all real and personal taxable property in the city. A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, and the city's rate sits beside county, school and special district lines on your notice.

The Property Appraiser publishes final millage sheets each year comparing the City of Tampa, Temple Terrace, Plant City and unincorporated Hillsborough County, and the 2026 sheet is posted on its Truth in Millage page. A turned-down exemption has its own 30 day clock from the mailing of the denial letter.

  • The homestead is available only where the owner lives in the home as a permanent resident on January 1.

Call the Property Appraiser at 813-272-6100 before the deadline if your notice looks wrong. A rental owner should also remember that renting a homesteaded home can end the exemption.

How does a sale change the tax on a Tampa house?

Buyers often pay more than sellers did. The county appraiser says homestead growth is capped at 3% a year, yet the capped value survives only through the year of purchase, after which the home is reassessed at market value. You may pay a pro-rated share of the seller's taxes at closing, yet the following year's assessment reflects the new market value.

State materials set the cap at the lower of 3% or the CPI change, and the sale counts as a change of ownership that resets the property on the next January 1. Buyers who ask what the seller pays are looking at a figure that will not carry over.

What do Tampa's neighborhoods and history mean for sellers?

Tampa's older areas were built in distinct waves, and age and location shape what buyers ask about. The city's history page says Fort Brooke was established in 1824, Henry B. Plant's railroad extension reached the Hillsborough River in 1884, and phosphate shipping and the 1886 cigar factory of Vicente Martinez Ybor shaped growth. Ybor City covers about two square miles between Nebraska Avenue, 22nd Street, Columbus Drive and East Broadway.

Ponce de Leon first reached the bay in 1513, and the area became part of the United States in 1845. The harbor and the Hillsborough River drive the local economy, and the city calls the convention center on the river, with its Riverwalk access, a downtown anchor. Tampa's main business district has grown considerably since the 1960s, with banks and corporations in towers above the bay, so downtown condos and townhomes sit in a different market than older bungalow streets.

A building boom from 1923 to 1926 produced many subdivisions, including Davis Island, a man-made island at the mouth of the Hillsborough River built by D.P. Davis. Today, MacDill Air Force Base houses U.S. Central Command and U.S. Special Operations Command, and the city's port is described as the seventh largest in the nation.

What does Florida charge at closing on a Tampa house?

The state deed tax is a documentary stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid through the clerk at recording. The statute leaves every party on the document answerable. Miami-Dade runs a different rate, which does not apply to Hillsborough.

  • Order a payoff for any unpaid tax year from the Tax Collector.
  • Ask the closing agent to prorate the current year's tax.
  • Keep a copy of the closing statement for your records.

Taxes that stay unpaid can reach a tax certificate sale. The certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years, so clear delinquent years before you accept an offer.

Can I sell my Tampa house if property taxes are behind?

Yes. The unpaid tax gets paid at closing, normally out of your proceeds. Request a payoff from the Hillsborough County Tax Collector and put it beside any mortgage payoff when you compare offers. A buyer who purchases as is can close without repairs, which helps when funds are tight.

The tax collector's office accepts payment online at HillsTaxFL.gov with a free e-Check, by mail, at 24/7 drop boxes and at service centers, so a seller who wants to clear the balance before listing has several routes. Ask for the exact payoff figure in writing.

The 2026 roll is due by March 31, 2027. Payment by November 30, 2026 saves 4%, December 31 saves 3%, January 31 saves 2% and February 28 saves 1%.

Phone the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser at 813-272-6100. Payment questions belong with the Tax Collector, 813-635-5200.

No. Only through the purchase year. After that the home is reassessed at market value, says the Property Appraiser.

Every party on the deed answers for it, whoever the contract names. The charge is 70 cents per $100, collected when the deed is recorded.

What makes Fort Lauderdale property different from the rest of Broward?

Water, mostly. The city counts 165 miles of inland waterways, which is how it earned the nickname "Venice of America," and boasts over 3,000 sunny hours yearly. Downtown also hosts Broward College, Florida Atlantic University, the Broward County Main Library, and federal, county and school district offices. Houses near water, and the condos along it, are the parcels the appraiser values most closely.

Why is the city called Fort Lauderdale, and how big is it?

From a Second Seminole War stockade built beside the New River in 1838. Major William Lauderdale led Tennessee Volunteers down the east coast that year, and three forts bore his name: one at the fork of the New River, one at Tarpon Bend and the largest on the beach where Bahia Mar sits now. None of them still stands.

The city incorporated on March 27, 1911. It covers roughly 36 square miles and, by the city's own estimate, about 186,220 people, making it the largest of Broward County's 31 municipalities and one of the ten largest in Florida.

QuickFacts shows 188,677 people as of July 2025, a 3.3 percent gain since 2020, and 80,999 households over 2020 to 2024. Housing details:

Start with a phone call, because clerical errors often get fixed informally. Failing that, file a petition with the clerk in the 25 days after the August notice. A denied exemption instead goes before the Value Adjustment Board, on a 30 day clock from the denial letter.

The Broward appraiser's home page tells buyers not to assume the seller's tax continues: a change of ownership resets assessed value to full market value. What you can carry is accumulated Save Our Homes savings, through portability to a new Florida homestead started inside a three year window; the appraiser offers a portability estimator for that. The closing agent prorates the year's tax. Separately, the appraiser runs a free Owner Alert that notifies you if a document changing ownership of your property reaches its office.

With the Broward appraiser, online or on paper. The on-time deadline is March 1, and 2027 late filings stop September 20, 2027.

Does the city assess my house?

No. Broward's appraiser values it and Broward's collector bills it; the city is only one of the taxing bodies listed.

Can I contest a Fort Lauderdale assessment?

Yes. Petition the clerk during the 25 days after the August notice, or use the Value Adjustment Board for a denied exemption. A call to the appraiser first often resolves errors.

Can renting out the house cost me the exemption?

It can. The exemption rests on permanent residence, so full-time rental use may end eligibility. Report changes in use to the appraiser.

Why does the age of West Palm Beach matter to a house seller?

The city started as a winter refuge for northerners, and its housing carries that layering. Its preservation office says early pioneer families arrived before 1900 to plant groves and fish, and that wealthy buyers on the island of Palm Beach created a service economy on the mainland. Incorporation came on November 5, 1894, with about 1,000 residents a year later.

The 1920s brought platted neighborhoods and a rush of speculative cottages and bungalows. Investor worry in 1926, material shortages, the 1928 hurricane and the Depression slowed that wave. World War II then drew soldiers to nearby bases, and many returned to build the postwar and midcentury infill that fills several neighborhoods today.

So a listing here can be a 1920s bungalow, a midcentury ranch or a newer place near the western preserve, and each one reaches the tax roll with a different value history. Read the parcel record before you trust any citywide figure.

Does a historic district change what I can do before selling?

It can, if the house sits inside one. The city counts 17 historic districts, nine of them on the National Register of Historic Places, plus more than 45 individually designated sites. The first preservation ordinance dates to November 26, 1990, after a survey that began in 1988.

  • Exterior changes to a designated property are reviewed by city staff or the Historic Preservation Board, depending on scope.
  • Historic approval has to come before any permit is issued for the work.
  • Routine upkeep that needs no permit, such as painting or minor exterior repair, skips extra review.

Yes, a city program in effect since February 14, 1994 exempts up to 100 percent of the added assessed value that comes from renovating a designated historic property. The exemption runs for ten years and covers interior or exterior work.

The city's own illustration is a house assessed at $250,000 whose new kitchen, bedroom suite and porch lift taxable value to $290,000. The $40,000 difference is then exempt from part of the ad valorem tax for the decade. The plans need Historic Preservation Board approval before work begins, and construction has to finish within two years of that approval, following the Secretary of the Interior's rehabilitation standards.

Income-producing buildings such as rentals can instead look at a 20 percent federal tax credit on rehabilitation costs, administered through the National Park Service. For a buyer comparing houses, an active exemption is worth asking about.

A 4 percent cut comes off November payments, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February.

  • Warranty, special warranty and quit claim deeds are taxable.

The city's own profile page, citing the Census Bureau, gives Pensacola 54,312 residents at the 2020 count, 22.67 square miles and household income at a median of $72,699 for 2019 to 2023. It also counts 5,334 veterans.

Spanish settlers under Don Tristan de Luna established the settlement in 1559, and the city calls itself America's First Settlement and the City of Five Flags. Naval Air Station Pensacola, the Blue Angels and Pensacola International Airport anchor local life, so military moves bring a steady flow of newcomers. Pensacola Beach lies on Santa Rosa Island, while Downtown Pensacola holds the historic district and Palafox Street.

The city profile also reports an average commute of 21.5 minutes, about 220 sunny days a year and a metro cost of living 5.80 percent under the national average, crediting FloridaWest. It counts more than 40 primary and secondary schools and says Pensacola International Airport serves over three million passengers a year. Those are points a buyer may weigh next to the tax bill.

Location inside the city can change the bill. The appraiser's millage page treats the Downtown Improvement Board as a separate authority and gives Pensacola Beach its own total. Bills go out in November. That same notice reports that voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026. It says the vote leaves the 2026 bill alone and that new homestead exemption amounts begin with the 2027 tax year.

Escambia also offers a quarterly plan to taxpayers whose prior year taxes topped $100 and who have no mortgage escrow. Sign up by April 30 of the year you want to use it. The collector prints this schedule.

  • Widow or widower: $5,000, supported by a death certificate.

Ask how the current year gets divided with the buyer. The buyer's first bill can look very different from yours. The sale resets the assessment to market value, so an asking price built around your old tax figure can mislead a buyer. Point them to the appraiser's record for the parcel.

  • Look up the deed history in the clerk's Official Records.

Yes, if last year's tax was over $100 and you have no escrow account. Apply by April 30; payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

Which offices bill Port St. Lucie property tax?

Port St. Lucie sits in St. Lucie County, so the county Property Appraiser values your house, the county Tax Collector mails the bill, and the Clerk of Court records the deed. The city levies only its own lines.

The county appraiser (paslc.gov) runs two offices: Fort Pierce at 2300 Virginia Avenue and Saint Lucie West at 250 NW Country Club Drive, both reachable at 772-462-1000. Its site has a tax estimator, an exemption filing portal, homestead portability information and a news item on getting a copy of a freshly recorded deed. The Tax Collector's site is tcslc.com, and the appraiser's government links list the Clerk of Court alongside the Sheriff and the Supervisor of Elections.

  • Property Appraiser: market and assessed value, exemptions, mailing address updates.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, partial payments, delinquent taxes.
  • City of Port St. Lucie: its own millage on the tax bill, set by the City Council.

What is the Port St. Lucie millage rate?

The city's pages list 4.8750 mills for FY 2026-27, down from 4.9750 in FY 2025-26. A mill is a dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of taxable value, so the city rate means $4.87 on every thousand.

The city's July 24, 2026 news release says the City Council approved the 4.8750 rate at its summer workshop on July 22 and 23, the 11th year in a row of cuts, with budget hearings on September 14 and 28 and the budget taking effect October 1, 2026. The city's tax page counts the drop from 6.6289 in FY 2015/16, and the release says the rate is down 25 percent since 2016 and has the third lowest municipal rate among Florida's 20 largest cities.

This is only one slice of your bill. City leaders say the council controls two lines, City of Port St. Lucie and the voter-approved debt for the Crosstown Parkway, which together make up 21 percent of a total bill. The other 14 lines belong to the county, school board, water management district and special districts. A bill can rise even when the city rate falls if your taxable value climbs faster, if another authority raises its rate, or if you lost an exemption.

When are St. Lucie County taxes due and can I pay in parts?

Bills are mailed on or about November 1, with a 4 percent discount for November payments, and the gross amount is due in March. Payments on or after April 1 are delinquent and penalized.

St. Lucie County Tax Collector payment options for Port St. Lucie parcels
OptionTerms as the Tax Collector prints them
Early discountNovember 4%, December 3%, January 2%, February 1%, none in March
Partial paymentsUp to 3, minimum $100 each, November through March, no discount
Installment planDue June 30 (6%), September 30 (4.5%), December 30 (3%), March 31 (no discount)
Installment eligibilityApplication closes April 30 of the plan year; estimated tax over $100; current year only

No partial payments are accepted after March 31. The collector's page says its window for 2027 installment applications opens November 1, 2026 and closes April 30, 2027, and that past due taxes cannot join the plan. Low-income homeowners with homestead can ask about the Homestead Tax Deferral Program, which postpones part of the tax based on household income.

What happens to delinquent Port St. Lucie property tax?

If the bill is not paid by March 31 it turns delinquent on April 1, and interest and fees start. Unpaid delinquent taxes go into the annual Tax Collector's certificate sale, which opens for bidding in May.

To stop a certificate, payment must arrive by five in the evening on the last business day ahead of June 1; certificates then issue on June 1 or the business day after it. Online payments shut off at that hour and reopen after processing, typically by mid-June. Payment counts when received, not when postmarked.

  • Accepted forms include cash, cashier's check, money order, wire, credit card, attorney trust check, title company check and mortgage escrow check.
  • Florida law does not let the collector take partial payments on delinquent taxes, though until a tax deed application is filed they can generally be paid one delinquent year at a time.
  • A certificate is not a loss of the house, but extra interest and fees apply, and the certificate can later support a tax deed application.

Someone else may pay a delinquent bill for you, and that payment gives them no ownership interest.

What does a sale do to the tax on a Port St. Lucie house?

A sale lets the appraiser reassess the house at full just value as of January 1 after the purchase and drop the seller's exemptions. The city's tax page uses a worked example of a 12-year owner whose assessed value was $110,000 and whose successor's came out at $130,000 on reassessment.

The previous owner's exemption and Save Our Homes benefit stay on the property through the calendar year of purchase, so a first bill can look lower than the one that follows. A buyer who lived in the home as of January 1 and files for homestead by March 1 gets the exemption that year, but the cap does not begin until the next year. The assessment cap, per the state revenue agency, is the lower of 3% or CPI, and the chart shows 2.7% for 2026.

On the closing side, The deed stamp rate is $0.70 for each $100 of price, and everyone named on the deed is liable for it. The Clerk collects it at recording. Have the closing agent order the tax payoff and confirm whether the current bill is settled.

How should a Port St. Lucie homeowner use homestead and portability?

A resident who owns and occupies the home as of January 1 can apply with the county appraiser by March 1 for homestead. The city's tax page says the first $25,000 applies to every levy, including school taxes, and the additional exemption applies only to non-school taxes.

Moving within Florida can bring a benefit: portability lets a homeowner transfer up to $500,000 of the Save Our Homes difference to a new homestead, inside a three year window counted from the January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up. The appraiser's site has a portability page and a TRIM notice explainer, and also a Report Homestead Fraud link.

The city's tax page also points to reductions for seniors, people with disabilities and veterans. If you own a Port St. Lucie rental or a house you moved out of, homestead ends once the unit is rented or no longer your permanent residence, so tell the appraiser rather than waiting for a review.

What should a Port St. Lucie seller check before closing?

Look up the parcel on the appraiser's site, confirm its exemption and value, and get the Tax Collector's balance for this year and any older years. Hand both to the closing agent.

If a bill is large because of a recent reassessment, ask whether the appraiser's tax estimator matches it. The estimator and TRIM notices are where the appraiser lists each authority's proposed rate before the final rates are certified in the fall. A value dispute is filed through the Value Adjustment Board forms on the appraiser's site, and the state revenue agency sets the petition window at 25 days after the TRIM notice goes out.

More questions about Port St. Lucie, FL Property Tax Guide

Who controls the Port St. Lucie tax rate?

The City Council sets only the city's own rate, which its pages list at 4.8750 mills for FY 2026-27. The county, school board and other authorities set the other lines on your bill.

What is the Port St. Lucie delinquency date?

April 1. St. Lucie County bills are due by March 31, and unpaid taxes are included in the certificate sale that opens in May.

Does Port St. Lucie allow installment payments?

Yes, through the St. Lucie County installment plan. The application closes April 30 and the estimated bill must top $100, and expect 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts on the first three payments.

How do I get the Port St. Lucie homestead exemption?

File with the St. Lucie County Property Appraiser by March 1, once you own the home and live in it on the January 1 assessment date. The appraiser has a File Online portal and two offices.

Does paying Port St. Lucie taxes late stop a certificate?

Only if the Tax Collector has it by five in the evening on the last business day ahead of June 1. A later payment cannot stop the certificate, even when mailed earlier.
